titleText.es: Hace poco uno me dijo que buscara un ordenador y lo encendiera para poder reiniciarlo. Se negaba a avanzar en su guión antes de que le dijera que había hecho eso.
titleText.en: I recently had someone ask me to go get a computer and turn it on so I could restart it. He refused to move further in the script until I said I had done that.
titleText.noteEn: These are the exact title texts from the Spanish archive and official xkcd metadata. The archive preserves the spelling guión used by the translator.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Teclea is a present form of teclear used for one person or thing, or for formal singular “you.” As a brief action label, it reports that one person is typing.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: to; with (introducing the destination of a phone transfer)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: After pasar in a telephone context, con introduces the person or department that the caller is put through to.

example.en: They put me through to reception.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins como mínimo, “at least”
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Como often means “as” or “like,” but in the fixed expression como mínimo it helps set a lower limit.

example.en: We need at least three chairs.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you intensify a Spanish description or quantity to mean “very” or “extremely”?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Replace the word's usual ending with the matching form -ísimo, -ísima, -ísimos, or -ísimas.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The ending matches the gender and number of what is described. For example, mucho becomes muchísimo, muchísima, muchísimos, or muchísimas. Some bases also change spelling or written stress, so common forms should be learned with their accents.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say “operating system” in Spanish?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Say sistema operativo; use sistemas operativos for more than one.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This is the conventional computing term. Sistema is masculine despite ending in -a, so operativo uses the masculine form and both words become plural together.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How can you reassure someone with “no problem”?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This conventional reply literally uses sin, “without,” plus problema. The plural sin problemas can instead describe doing something without difficulties.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something may happen at any time?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: En introduces a point in time, and cualquier before the singular noun momento leaves that point unrestricted.

example.en: You can call at any time.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you name a technical support or repair service?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: This conventional term can refer to technical support or to a service that diagnoses and repairs products. Técnico follows servicio and matches its masculine singular form.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: Say lenguaje de programación; use lenguajes de programación for more than one.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De programación identifies the field or purpose of the language. Only lenguaje changes to mark the plural.

example.es: Python es un lenguaje de programación.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you name support that is provided by telephone?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Telefónico follows soporte and identifies the channel used for the support. It changes to match another noun when needed, as in asistencia telefónica.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: pasar a alguien con otra persona (por teléfono)
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that a caller is put through to another person or department?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of pasar for the transfer, then con before the person or department reached.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Pasar changes for the person and time. The caller may appear as a short pronoun, as in me pasaron con ventas, while con introduces the destination of the telephone transfer.

example.en: Can you put me through to sales?

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is farther away or beyond a point?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use más allá; add de before a named reference point.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Más allá works as a fixed place expression. It can stand alone for “farther away,” or appear as más allá de followed by the place, limit, or idea that is exceeded.

example.es: El pueblo está más allá de la colina.
example.en: The town is beyond the hill.
